articles.title: State Bank of India (SBI) Bandwar Branch: IFSC & Services
articles.subtitle: The village's only bank branch and a lifeline for local farmers
articles.summary: The Bandwar branch of the State Bank of India (IFSC: SBIN0015585) is the only formal banking facility in the village. Located near the [[shaheed-ramchandra-dwar-bandwar|Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar]] on the main Bandwar Road, it serves not just the village but also the surrounding panchayats. From handling MGNREGA wages to providing Kisan Credit Cards for local farmers, the branch is a crucial link between Bandwar and the formal economy.

photos.caption: The SBI Bandwar branch building in 2015.
The SBI Bandwar branch in 2026, after renovation.
The 24/7 SBI ATM at the Bandwar branch.

infobox.Services: Savings, KCC Loans, NEFT/RTGS/UPI, Lockers, Govt. DBTs

content.heading: Overview
content.text: The State Bank of India branch in Bandwar is a lifeline for the village. Standing on the main Bandwar Road near the Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar, it is often the first institutional building a visitor sees when entering the village. Before this branch opened, residents had to travel to Begusarai or Barauni — a costly and time-consuming journey — for basic tasks like opening an account or withdrawing cash. Today, it serves not only Bandwar but also the adjoining panchayats, acting as a financial hub for the rural population.

content.heading: Financial Inclusion and Farmers
content.text: The branch plays a massive role in financial inclusion. Since Bandwar is an agricultural village, the bank is deeply integrated with the farming cycle. Many farmers in the village utilize Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) from this branch to purchase seeds, fertilizers, and to hire tractors for their fields. During the harvest season, the bank sees a heavy footfall as farmers deposit their earnings. Furthermore, the branch is the nodal point for Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT), ensuring that MGNREGA wages, old-age pensions, and PM-Kisan installments reach the villagers directly without middlemen.

content.heading: Renovation and Modernisation
content.text: The branch has evolved with time. Between 2015 and 2025, the branch underwent a major renovation. The old beige exterior was replaced with a modern blue and white colour scheme, and the interiors were upgraded with new computers, improved seating, and an updated security system. The bank also installed a dedicated ATM, which remains busy 24/7. For a village, the ATM is a boon during late nights or emergencies when the bank is closed.

content.heading: Daily Reality at the Branch
content.text: The daily reality of the branch is defined by the local people. On pension days or when MGNREGA wages are released, long queues of elderly men and women form outside the gates. The staff, many of whom are locals or have served here for years, know the villagers by name. Despite the rise of digital banking, a significant portion of Bandwar's population still relies on passbook entries and cash withdrawals, making the physical branch indispensable.

faqs.q: What is the IFSC code of the SBI Bandwar branch?
faqs.a: The IFSC code of the State Bank of India's Bandwar branch is SBIN0015585.

faqs.q: Does the SBI branch help local farmers?
faqs.a: Yes, the branch issues Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) which help local farmers from Bandwar buy seeds, fertilizers, and equipment for their agricultural needs.

faqs.q: Are government pensions available at this bank?
faqs.a: Yes, the branch facilitates Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) for government schemes, including MGNREGA wages and old-age pensions.

faqs.q: Does the SBI Bandwar branch have an ATM?
faqs.a: Yes, there is a 24/7 SBI ATM at the branch, which is heavily used by villagers and people from nearby areas.

articles.title: Banduar Post Office (PIN 851131): Village Postal Hub
articles.subtitle: The branch post office and the postman's daily round in Bandwar
articles.summary: Banduar Branch Office is the village's post office, operating under the Begusarai postal division. It provides letter mail, registered post, money orders, and savings bank services. For families whose members work in cities like Delhi, Punjab, or Gujarat, the post office is the traditional bridge for communication and remittances.

photos.caption: The Banduar Branch Post Office serving Bandwar village.

infobox.Services: Letter mail, registered post, money orders, Aadhaar, Savings

content.heading: Overview
content.text: Located a short walk from the SBI branch and the Shaheed Dwar, the Banduar Branch Office is an integral part of Bandwar's daily life. It is a small facility, but its role is outsize. In rural Bihar, the post office is not just for letters; it is a bank, a government service center, and a communication hub. It serves Bandwar and the nearby panchayats under the Rajaura Sub Office.

content.heading: The Postman: The Village's Messenger
content.text: The most important figure in the post office is the postman (Dak-harkara). Every morning, he sets out on his bicycle, carrying a canvas bag filled with letters, parcels, and money orders. Because many families in Bandwar have members working as migrant labourers in other states, the postman is often the bearer of important news — a money order for a festival, a letter from a son, or an examination result. In the age of WhatsApp, the physical letter may have decreased, but the postman's arrival is still awaited.

content.heading: Money Orders and Aadhaar
content.text: For decades, the money order was the lifeline of rural Bihar. While bank transfers (UPI) have become common, many older residents still prefer the reliability of the post office. The Banduar BO handles a steady stream of money orders. Additionally, the post office acts as an Aadhaar enrolment and update centre. Villagers come here to link their Aadhaar with government schemes or to register for new connections.

content.heading: The PIN Code 851131
content.text: Bandwar falls under PIN code 851131. For any online order, government application, or official letter, this six-digit code is the village's identity. The post office ensures that essential documents — from exam admit cards to land registry papers — are delivered securely to the correct households.

faqs.q: What is Bandwar's PIN code?
faqs.a: Bandwar's PIN code is 851131, which comes under the Begusarai postal division.

faqs.q: What is the Banduar Branch Office?
faqs.a: It is the village post office of Bandwar, operating as a Branch Office (BO) under the Rajaura Sub Office.

faqs.q: Are money orders still used in Bandwar?
faqs.a: Yes, while UPI is growing, many older residents still rely on money orders sent by family members working in other states, as they find it more reliable.

faqs.q: Can I get Aadhaar work done at the post office?
faqs.a: Yes, the Banduar BO facilitates Aadhaar enrolment and updates for villagers.

articles.title: Ram Janki Fuels: Indian Oil Petrol Pump on SH 55
articles.subtitle: The primary fuel station serving Bandwar and highway traffic
articles.summary: Ram Janki Fuels is an Indian Oil petrol pump operating on SH 55 near Bandwar. It is the only petrol pump in the immediate area and serves both the village and passing highway traffic. It represents one of the few organised-sector employment opportunities available locally, and stands as a marker of the region's improving connectivity.

photos.caption: Ram Janki Fuels, the Indian Oil petrol pump on SH 55 near Bandwar.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: Ram Janki Fuels is a modern Indian Oil outlet located on State Highway 55 (SH 55) near Bandwar. With its tall canopy, four filling stations, and clear signage, it is a prominent landmark on the highway. For the villagers, it is a reliable place to fuel their motorcycles, tractors, and generator sets without having to go all the way to Begusarai town.

content.heading: A Hub for Highway Traffic
content.text: Because it sits directly on SH 55, the pump's main customers are not just locals, but also trucks, buses, and private cars traveling to and from Begusarai. The pump's forecourt often serves as a resting point. Drivers stop here to refuel, check their tyres, and grab a quick cup of tea from the small stalls that have sprung up nearby. This constant flow of traffic brings a small but steady economic boost to the area.

content.heading: Fueling Agriculture
content.text: In an agricultural village like Bandwar, the petrol pump plays a vital role during the harvest season. Farmers rely on diesel to run tractors, water pumps for irrigation, and threshing machines. During the peak agricultural months, the pump sees a rush of tractor owners filling up their tanks. The availability of Servo lubricants at the pump also helps local mechanics maintain agricultural machinery.

content.heading: Employment and Local Economy
content.text: The pump employs a small team of local workers. For these young men, working at the fuel station provides a fixed, non-agricultural income — a rare opportunity in the village. The pump also acts as a small economic node; the presence of the station encourages local vendors to sell snacks, tea, and basic vehicle spare parts nearby, creating a micro-economy right on the highway. It is a clear sign of how the village's infrastructure is slowly modernizing.

faqs.q: What is the name of the petrol pump near Bandwar?
faqs.a: The petrol pump is called Ram Janki Fuels. It is an Indian Oil dealer located on State Highway 55 (SH 55).

faqs.q: Is Ram Janki Fuels important for local farmers?
faqs.a: Yes, during harvest and sowing seasons, local farmers heavily rely on the pump for diesel to run their tractors and irrigation pumps.

faqs.q: Does the pump serve highway traffic?
faqs.a: Yes, because it is on SH 55, it serves trucks, buses, and cars traveling to and from Begusarai and other towns, acting as a convenient resting stop.

faqs.q: Does Ram Janki Fuels provide employment to locals?
faqs.a: Yes, the pump employs local youth as attendants and staff, providing a steady source of income away from traditional farming.

articles.title: Jal Jeevan Mission Water Tower: Piped Water in Bandwar
articles.subtitle: The infrastructure that changed the village's water landscape
articles.summary: A water tower built near Bandwar under the central government's Jal Jeevan Mission. It stands near the [[bandh-embankment-bandwar|bandh]] along the [[burhi-gandak-river-bandwar|Burhi Gandak]], drawing on the local groundwater. The tower is part of a massive effort to bring piped drinking water to households that previously relied entirely on hand-pumps and wells.

photos.caption: The Jal Jeevan Mission water tower near the Bandwar embankment.

infobox.Groundwater Issue: High iron content in some areas

content.heading: Overview
content.text: The Jal Jeevan Mission water tower is one of the most visible modern structures in Bandwar. The blue and white steel frame, topped with large black water tanks, stands on the edge of the village near the embankment of the Burhi Gandak river. It represents a fundamental shift in how the village accesses water. Until recently, women and children had to manually operate hand-pumps or draw water from open wells, a task that was both physically demanding and often unsafe.

content.heading: The Shift to Piped Water
content.text: The 2011 Census recorded zero households in Bandwar with piped water connections. The Jal Jeevan Mission aims to change this entirely. The tower pumps groundwater, treats it, and distributes it through a network of pipes laid under the village roads. For households that have received connections, turning on a tap has replaced the daily drudgery of carrying heavy pitchers. This has had a disproportionate benefit for the women of Bandwar, saving them hours of labour every day.

content.heading: Water Quality and the Iron Issue
content.text: Groundwater in parts of Begusarai district often has a high iron content. While the water from the tower is treated, the transition has not been without challenges. Some villagers note that the taste of piped water is different from the sweet water of their old, deep hand-pumps. Additionally, the pipeline network has faced issues with maintenance and irregular supply in some pockets, requiring constant coordination between the village and the Public Health Engineering Department (PHED).

content.heading: The 2025 Diarrhea Outbreak Connection
content.text: The importance of this tower is best understood in the context of the [[diarrhea-outbreak-bandwar-september-2025|September 2025 diarrhea outbreak]]. Before the piped water reached the Mahadalit basti (Wards 1 and 2), residents relied on shallow hand-pumps that were easily contaminated by floodwaters and poor sanitation. The outbreak, which claimed over ten lives, was a direct result of this water insecurity. The expansion of the Jal Jeevan pipeline to these wards became a top priority for the community after the tragedy.

faqs.q: What is the Jal Jeevan Mission?
faqs.a: It is a central government scheme launched in 2019 to provide safe, piped drinking water to every rural household in India. The water tower in Bandwar is a result of this scheme.

faqs.q: Where is the water tower located in Bandwar?
faqs.a: The tower is located on the edge of the village fields, near the embankment (bandh) of the Burhi Gandak river.

faqs.q: Did this tower prevent the 2025 diarrhea outbreak?
faqs.a: Not completely. The pipeline had not yet reached the most affected wards (1 and 2) at the time of the outbreak. The tragedy highlighted the urgent need to connect every household to the clean water grid.

faqs.q: What was used before this water tower?
faqs.a: Before the Jal Jeevan Mission, the village relied entirely on hand-pumps and traditional wells for all its drinking and household water needs.

articles.title: Roads & Connectivity in Bandwar: SH 55 and Village Lanes
articles.subtitle: How the village connects to Begusarai and the world
articles.summary: Bandwar is connected to the wider region by SH 55, by a network of village roads, and by a series of new road projects sanctioned in 2025. The village's isolation has reduced significantly in recent years, and the road network is one of the most important factors in the village's economic and social life.

photos.caption: Bricks and timber on a village road in Bandwar.
A village lane with bamboo fencing in Musahri tola.

content.heading: SH 55: The Main Artery
content.text: State Highway 55 is the lifeline of Bandwar. It passes right through the village, connecting it to Begusarai town (18 km away) and beyond. The highway is busy with a mix of local auto-rickshaws (e-rickshaws), private motorcycles, agricultural tractors, and heavy trucks carrying goods. The presence of the [[ram-janki-petrol-pump-bandwar|Ram Janki Fuels]] on this road has made the junction a natural stopping point for travelers.

content.heading: Village Lanes and the Monsoon Challenge
content.text: While SH 55 is paved, the internal roads and lanes of Bandwar tell a different story. Many of the residential lanes, especially towards the Musahri tola, are unpaved (kutcha) or paved with interlocking bricks. During the monsoon season, these lanes become muddy and difficult to navigate for two-wheelers. The village relies heavily on e-rickshaws (locally called autos) for last-mile connectivity, which often struggle through the potholes during the rains.

content.heading: The 2025 Road Projects
content.text: A major boost came in 2025 when administrative approval was granted for eight road projects affecting Bandwar and neighboring panchayats. The most crucial for the village is the road from the Gandak Bandh to Bandwar Mushahri. This route is vital as it provides direct road access to the [[gps-bandwar-musahri-school|Musahri tola school]] and the densely populated surrounding habitation. Improving this road means children can reach school more easily during the monsoon, and emergency vehicles can access the area.

content.heading: The Chhatauna Bridge
content.text: The Chhatauna Bridge over the Burhi Gandak is a critical link connecting Bandwar to the northern bank of the river. However, its narrow, single-lane structure and the deteriorating approach road create bottlenecks. During the flood season, when the river swells, the bridge becomes a point of high vigilance. Villagers frequently demand the widening and repair of the approach road for safer transport.

faqs.q: What is the main road connecting Bandwar to the region?
faqs.a: State Highway 55 (SH 55) is the main road connecting Bandwar to Begusarai and beyond. It is the primary route for buses and private vehicles.

faqs.q: How far is Bandwar from Begusarai town?
faqs.a: Bandwar is approximately 18 kilometres from Begusarai town, the district headquarters.

faqs.q: What new road projects have been sanctioned for Bandwar?
faqs.a: In 2025, approvals were granted for roads including the Gandak Bandh to Bandwar Mushahri road, improving access to the Musahri tola school, along with other regional projects.

faqs.q: What is the condition of roads inside the village?
faqs.a: While the main highway is good, many internal lanes are unpaved or made of interlocking bricks, which can become muddy and difficult to navigate during the monsoon.
